title: Single-thread baseline measurement on simulation.rs run_with_decoder
description:
## Goal

Produce the canonical single-thread throughput baseline against which
every `parallelism-pays`-gated task in the epic measures its speedup
claim. The baseline is measured on the legacy
`crates/gf2-coding/src/simulation.rs::SimulationRunner::run_with_decoder`
path (the path being migrated by `bbf6b6ee`), so the receipts in
`dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/parallelism-receipts.md` compare new-pipeline
parallel runs against the system they're meant to replace, not against
the new pipeline running on one thread (which would be a useless
self-comparison).

## Context

Task under story `bcf7776d` (CPU foundation for gf2-sim pipeline)
within epic `gf2-sim` (`f9717e7e`). Filed during the 2026-06-07
adversarial-review remediation per audit finding H8 ("no benchmark
baseline task"). Sequencing: depends on `ec530af9` (Phase 0 design
doc) so the measurement methodology aligns with the contract;
`3fcb7025` (within-SNR parallelism) depends on this so its
`parallelism-pays` receipt has a canonical denominator.

The 2026-06-05 campaign attempt produced an opportunistic
single-thread number: 1.617 frames/sec for r1/2 16-QAM,
n_ldpc=64800, SumProduct + ExactLogMap, Es/N0=6.25 dB, on AMD Ryzen
9 5900X, host `/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/gf2`. That number drove the
adversarial review's feasibility math. This task replaces the
opportunistic measurement with a repeatable, multi-configuration
matrix.

## Deliverables

1. Baseline harness in `crates/gf2-sim/benches/baseline_single_thread.rs`
   or `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/baseline_runner/` that:
   - Invokes `SimulationRunner::run_with_decoder` on the legacy
     `simulation.rs` path (no new code in `gf2-sim` is exercised).
   - Pins the run to one thread (e.g. via
     `rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::num_threads(1)` if the path uses
     rayon, or by direct single-thread invocation).
   - Sweeps the following matrix and records (frames/sec, mean_iters,
     wall_seconds, ber, fer) per cell:
     - 3 DVB-T2 MODCODs covering both modulations: r1/2 16-QAM,
       r2/3 16-QAM, r1/2 64-QAM.
     - 3 Es/N0 points per MODCOD, one each near {pre-waterfall,
       waterfall-mid, deep-waterfall} as identified by the existing
       `dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/smoke/` results.
     - Decoder × demap pairs: (SumProduct, ExactLogMap),
       (NormalizedMinSum(0.75), ExactLogMap), (MinSum, MaxLog).
     - Fixed seed `--seed 42`. 200 frames per cell (matches existing
       smoke).
2. Output: `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/baseline-single-thread.csv` with
   columns: `rate, modulation, es_n0_db, decoder, demap, frames,
   wall_seconds, frames_per_sec, mean_iters, ber, fer, commit_sha,
   date`.
3. Receipt note: `dev/benchmarks/gf2-sim/baseline-single-thread.md`
   summarising hardware (CPU model, threads, RAM, OS, rustc version),
   methodology, and the headline table. The note is the canonical
   reference cited by every `parallelism-pays` receipt that says
   "baseline single-thread" or "baseline single-host."

## Success Criteria

- [hard] CSV produced at the path above, ≥ 27 rows
  (3 MODCODs × 3 SNRs × 3 decoder/demap pairs).
- [hard] Receipt note produced at the path above; cites commit SHA,
  invocation, and the headline frames/sec for the canonical
  configuration (r1/2 16-QAM, Es/N0 = 6.25 dB, SumProduct,
  ExactLogMap) within ± 10 % of the prior opportunistic 1.6 fps
  figure (sanity check; large drift indicates the harness is not
  measuring the path the audit math assumed).
- [hard] Harness reusable: the same binary or bench, invoked at a
  later commit, reproduces the matrix and emits a delta vs the
  committed CSV. (The receipt note documents how.)
- [hard] No new `unsafe`; satisfies `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` if the
  harness lives inside `gf2-sim`.
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- This task does NOT modify `simulation.rs`.
- This task does NOT exercise any GPU path.
- This task does NOT bracket the FER waterfall to 10⁻⁴ — that is
  the production sweep owned by `e4849f07`.
- The 200-frames-per-cell granularity is intentional: this is a
  *throughput* baseline, not an *accuracy* baseline.
